what_happened: A retry (qb41) of the firstmate re-study also asked for a code check. Athena read the combined request as a change to the system's capability, so the job had no pinned firstmate source to study. The operator did not retry again. They asked for the re-study alone as a study-only job. No job is attached to this event.
cause: Athena gives each request one work type, and that type decides what inputs are prepared, such as pinning the source to study. A request that mixes two kinds of work is forced into one type, and the code-change reading wins. Nothing detects the mix, splits it, or asks. Retry reuses the same request text and the same classification, so it repeats the misreading. The operator can only escape by re-asking outside the retry path. This is the same missing recovery path seen in the earlier stuck re-study job.
prevention: At intake, detect requests that combine study work with code work. Split them into a study job and a separate code-check job that depends on it. Pin the study source whenever any part of the request is a study, whatever type the whole request gets. Let retry re-run intake classification, or take a corrected type, so the operator does not need to resubmit.
proposed_request: Re-study firstmate as a study-only job. Pin the current firstmate source at the start, and produce the study output with no code changes. Do not bundle any code check. I will request the code check as a separate job once the study is accepted.
